clue.text: Outstanding dispute not allowed in court

parts.note: outstanding means foremost, top of the field, i.e. leading
to dispute something is to question it; a dispute is a question at issue

explanation.surface: A row that has not been settled is barred from being heard by the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrister may not ask a witness a question that suggests the answer it wants; the judge disallows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A question that prompts the desired reply is ruled improper in a courtroom examination of witnesses.

clue.text: Shoot winner with lead excitedly, then relax

indicators.note: done excitedly, the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fire at the champion who is in front in a frenzy, and then take it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'excitedly' rearranges the fifteen letters of SHOOT, WINNER and LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for abandoning restraint and enjoying yourself, taken from loosening pinned-up hair.

clue.text: Turn aside right after the avenue

indicators.note: right comes after the avenue, so its letters follow in the answer

explanation.surface: Directions to swerve to the right once you pass the avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert is to turn something away, as in averting your eyes.

clue.text: Trendy, elevating one with help when in a state

parts.note: trendy means fashionable, in

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevating lifts these pieces so they read bottom to top

parts.note: AN is the article meaning one
aid is help

explanation.surface: Someone fashionable lifting a person with assistance while in some region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevating' works only because this is a down entry: the reversed run DIANA reads like a woman's name, a helpful check.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: It's almost grim to sell up screens

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word grim loses its final letter
in a down clue, up means the word sell is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Selling things up, i.e. disposing of everything, is nearly a grim business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims GRIM to GRI and 'up' turns SELL into LLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Grilles are latticed screens over windows or openings.

clue.text: Dangerous vessel, one with a foul appearance

parts.note: ugly can mean threatening or dangerous, as in an ugly mood
a mug is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A hazardous ship belonging to someone of grim aspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly mug is slang for a person whose face is unattractive.

clue.text: Society friend embraces her, being perfectly round

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the friend's letters surround the next word

parts.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written

explanation.surface: A society companion hugs a woman, who is extremely plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheral means shaped like a sphere, perfectly round.

clue.text: Route: it gets in on time by railway

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A travel plan in which the train arrives punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerary is a planned route or schedule for a journey.

clue.text: Unprepossessing, like a small portion

definitions.meaning: a meagre helping offers little to see on the plate

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for plain-looking, and literally describes a tiny serving.

clue.text: It's monotonous to half study a philosopher

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word to keeps just its first letter

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher

explanation.surface: Studying a thinker part-time is a dull task.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: a treadmill is anything dully repetitive.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill figuratively means a tedious, repetitive routine.

clue.text: Unnatural is the hold-up

indicators.note: unnatural means not in the normal state, so the letters are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: A robbery is not natural behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up is a robbery, and so is a heist.

clue.text: Activity involving latticework, black completely

parts.note: a net is a mesh, a kind of latticework
B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black
all can mean completely, as in all wrong

explanation.surface: A pastime involving trelliswork that is entirely black.
explanation.walkthrough: NETBALL is a team sport like basketball, widely played in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a sport, a team activity played with a ball and raised hoops.

clue.text: Doctor with a cure composed a piece of music

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of a cure are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A physician with a remedy wrote some music.
explanation.definitionFit: Morceau is French for a short piece, used for a short musical composition.

clue.text: Caught in the mud, I can't fly

indicators.note: letters caught in these words are held within them

explanation.surface: A creature stuck in mud complains it cannot take off.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless bird, so it speaks the definition in the first person.

clue.text: Screws in petticoats gripping a queen's back

indicators.note: back sends the whole assembly the other way round
gripping means holding inside, so the petticoats surround the next pieces

parts.note: slips are petticoats
R, for regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Bolts concealed in underskirts clinging to a royal's back.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIPS gripping A and R gives SLARIPS; 'back' reverses all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirals and screws are both helical; a screw is a spiral thread, and screws can mean spirals.

clue.text: Uncertain view of an ignoramus?

parts.note: the stock reply of someone unsure, and also the constant reply of a person who knows nothing

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase states uncertainty and is what someone ignorant says to every question.

clue.text: Short flower girl goes up and down

indicators.note: reads the same going up as coming down the grid
short means cut down, so the flower loses its last letter

parts.note: a lily is a flower

explanation.surface: A small flower-seller bobs about.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortened LILY gives a girl's name that reads the same upward or downward.
explanation.definitionFit: Lil is a girl's name, a short form of Lilian.

clue.text: Giant porker swallows tail when retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, reversing the whole
swallows means takes inside, so the porker holds the next word

parts.note: a hog is a porker, a pig

explanation.surface: A pig gulps down its own tail as it backs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when retreating' reverses the whole container, giving the giant slain by David; 'Giant' is a definition, not an adjective for the pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the biblical giant felled by David, now a byword for any giant.

clue.text: Whole sole

definitions.meaning: a whole is a single unit, a unity

explanation.definitionFit: One means a single complete unit and also only, as in the one person.

clue.text: Preacher leaps to conclusion

indicators.note: leaps to a conclusion suggests jumping wildly, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A churchman judges hastily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusion' signals the anagram of LEAPS TO, with the surface's 'leaps to conclusion' meaning judges hastily.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a missionary who spreads the faith, a preacher.

clue.text: Location of some wet fielders?

parts.note: deep is a cricket fielding area far from the batsman, and also a poetic name for the sea where things are wet

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders stationed near the boundary are 'in the deep'; the ocean is also called this.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea, poetically, is where fielders placed far out would be soaked.

clue.text: Was kinder, supplying relief and turnover pudding

parts.note: ease is relief from pain or worry

indicators.note: turnover means turned over, so the pudding reads upward in this down clue

parts.note: pud is a British informal word for pudding

explanation.surface: Someone gentler offers comfort along with an apple turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: A turnover is also a pastry, which suits the dessert in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease up is to relax pressure, to be less harsh or more lenient.

clue.text: Answer from salesman having left broken toy

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: broken means smashed, so the letters of toy are reassembled

explanation.surface: A salesman's response, having abandoned a broken plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: To reply to a letter is to answer it.

clue.text: Perhaps RNLI reserve gets sign right

parts.note: a cue is a sign or signal

explanation.surface: A lifeboat volunteer on standby gets a signal to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: The RNLI is Britain's Royal National Lifeboat Institution, a rescue charity.
explanation.definitionFit: The lifeboat service is an example of a rescuer, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: See slip loose inside fur-trimmed cloak

indicators.note: set loose inside, the letters break free and regroup

explanation.surface: Look, a slip worn under a cloak edged with fur.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelisse is a long cloak or coat lined or trimmed with fur.

clue.text: Wonder how a week has half gone

indicators.note: with half gone, only the first half of the word week is left

explanation.surface: Amazement at how half a week has passed already.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is a feeling of wonder mixed with reverence.

clue.text: Horses won't start for unkind people

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter is missing

parts.note: trotters are horses bred for trotting races

explanation.surface: Racehorses refuse to begin, to the annoyance of nasty folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotters is dated British slang for cads, nasty people.

clue.text: Abroad, learns nothing in Italy

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or widely scattered, so the letters wander

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An overseas student picks up nothing while in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the place itself, 'in Italy' standing for a city there.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno is a port city in southern Italy.

clue.text: Showing one horn, perhaps

parts.note: the Indian and Javan species of this large beast have a single horn on the nose

explanation.definitionFit: Some rhinoceros species bear a single horn, so one shows one horn, perhaps.

clue.text: Animal once seen circling university

indicators.note: circling means surrounding, so the word once goes round the next letter

explanation.surface: A creature once spotted prowling round a campus.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat.

clue.text: Sleuth goes round Queer Street to get some chicken

indicators.note: goes round means surrounds, so the sleuth's letters enclose the next pieces

parts.note: a dick is slang for a detective
rum means odd or queer in old British slang

explanation.surface: A detective visits a strange road to fetch a bit of poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: Queer Street is old British slang for being in debt, adding colour to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A drumstick is the lower leg of a cooked chicken, one part of it.

clue.text: A piece of rag?

parts.note: rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper, and a piece is an article printed in one

explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper, so a piece in it is an article.
